title: Prevent signed request replay after nonce eviction
summary: Retain authenticated request nonces for the full timestamp-validity window and fail closed when the live nonce cache reaches its fixed capacity.
reason: Remediate P1 AUDIT-FIND-W01-010. A request signed at the positive clock-skew boundary could outlive its nonce entry and execute the same coordinator mutation a second time.
behavior_before: Accepted nonces expired at acceptance-time plus one skew interval, even when a future timestamp remained admissible beyond that expiry; the cache also had no fixed admission bound.
behavior_after: Accepted nonces expire no earlier than max(acceptance time, signed timestamp) plus the skew interval, expired entries are pruned first, and a full cache rejects new authentication attempts without evicting any still-valid nonce.
tests_added: tests/python/desktop/test_network_security.py: deterministic future-timestamp nonce retention, capacity fail-closed behavior, and live coordinator HTTP replay rejection for an identical signed mutation.

notes: Finding disposition: AUDIT-FIND-W01-010 is remediated and independently validated against current source, pre-fix red evidence, deterministic clock/cache fixtures, a live localhost coordinator HTTP mutation, the full network suite, and full desktop baseline classification. Python impact: coordinator HMAC authentication only; route payloads and media policy are unchanged. The 10,000-entry bound rejects new unique nonces only after pruning expired entries, so live replay evidence is never discarded to make room. The separate core/network/auth.py duplicate is not on the coordinator request-validation path and remains outside this finding-scoped packet. Representative real-media validation is not required.
